policy_binding.method: Each app's eleven unique uppercase SPKI SHA-256 values must exactly equal the canonical policy key set; tests compare keys, not checkout bytes.

design.ca-copy: Runs only /bin/sh in the exact original pinned application image, copying public OS trust trees and complete known certifi packages into a fresh emptyDir. No user config/media mounts.
design.ca-filter: Runs stock Python with bytecode disabled against that isolated snapshot. Bazarr and SABnzbd use their original application images; Prowlarr uses the already pinned Bazarr vendor image because Prowlarr has neither Python nor OpenSSL CLI.
design.fail_closed: Kubernetes must complete the ordinary ca-copy and ca-filter init containers before any original application container starts. No custom-cont-init.d hook, s6 failure propagation assumption or fallback is used.
design.main: Original vendor /init, application image/version, environment, auth/data initialization, probes, PVC mounts and SAB codec configuration command are retained. Main container receives only read-only trust overlays.
design.immutability: Mount whole OS source directories, hash directory/bundle, and entire application/pip certifi packages read-only. Do not use environment-only CA redirection or file-only certifi mounts that leave package replacement unguarded.
design.hash_directories: Remove denied aliases and compact surviving vendor subject-hash sequences to avoid OpenSSL lookup gaps. Preserve unaffected certificate DER identities; reject escaping/dangling/cyclic/unsupported aliases.
design.updates: One shared base at apps/_shared/media-ca-hardening generates ca-guard from the sole script/copy/policy files. Each app's ca-guard child Kustomization prefixes only that base. App-specific hashed ConfigMap names are transformed into HelmRelease persistence references, so script/policy changes alter pod volume references without prefixing application resources.
design.dependencies: Guard uses only stock Python standard-library ssl/base64/hashlib and a bounded DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo parser. No newly built/maintained images, package installs, downloads, TLS bypass or compiled helpers.
design.sab_codec_init: Original codec-config command/image/data mounts are unchanged; it runs after the two CA init containers and receives the same read-only sanitized trust overlays.

prowlarr.filter_helper: Exact same Bazarr index/amd64 child recorded above; it never runs vendor /init or makes network requests.
prowlarr.native_runtime: .NET 8.0.27; stock native OpenSSL library; no Python/OpenSSL CLI

vendor_init_findings: All stock image entrypoints are /init. Default /etc/ssl/cert.pem is a relative alias to certs/ca-certificates.crt, covered by the read-only cert-directory overlay.
Public pinned-image s6 init/service/dependency scripts, docker-mods, migration/preinit scripts and known trust paths were inspected without executing images.
init-custom-files/run echoes the custom script exit code and continues, so it cannot gate original application startup.
Existing init-mods-package-install/run can invoke apk/apt/pip and regenerate packages/trust. No such installers are added or invoked by either CA initializer.

SAB's existing pinned universal-package-install mod and INSTALL_PACKAGES=ffmpeg are preserved. Their real interaction with read-only trust directories remains an explicit deployment blocker until isolated Linux validation.

Read-only whole-directory/package overlays are intended to prevent later init/mod stages from overwriting or replacing sanitized stores; actual Linux mount enforcement and complete vendor bootstrap are not yet verified.
verified_preparation: Independent cryptography SPKI hashes match the stdlib parser across all inspected real vendor PEM stores: Bazarr 124 stores / 3 baseline denied copies, Prowlarr 122 / 2, SABnzbd 121 / 1.

Fixture tests cover exact-key rather than subject matching, malformed/partial policies and bundles, source/bundle/application filtering, unaffected-root preservation, hash-sequence compaction and idempotent read-only verification.

Native Windows Python/OpenSSL memory-BIO TLS controls accept an unaffected synthetic fixture root after filtering and reject the removed synthetic fixture root. This does not certify stock Linux application/native/custom TLS.
Helm app-template 5.2.1 renders ca-copy then ca-filter, before original codec-config where present. New CA initializers have no config/media PVC mounts.
Hashed ConfigMap references render correctly for all three app Kustomizations.
Existing SAB codec/bootstrap, shared media codec policy and Servarr HTTPS regressions pass.
remaining_blockers: Local Windows execution lacks Docker/WSL. Coordinator has an authorized GitHub-hosted Linux/Docker runner through held draft PR326; media execution there is pending, not permanently unavailable. Real pinned-image execution, Linux absolute-alias tests, mount enforcement and stock /init readiness tests are NOT run in this worktree.
Run the explicit --docker suite on isolated linux/amd64 Docker 26+ (volume-subpath support), with network disabled during execution and no user config/media. Images may be pulled before execution.

The Docker suite tests base vendor bootstrap without downloading SAB's optional mod; a complete replay of the already-existing pinned ffmpeg mod/package stage must also establish compatibility before deployment.

No .NET cached/user-added/custom/compiled certificate-store or chain-validation certification is claimed. Actual live public-store and native/application rejection verification is still required after separately authorized deployment.
Another session owns Longhorn repair. No storage diagnosis/changes or deployment is part of this preparation.

sab_complete_mod_acceptance.existing_docker_suite_limit: The current --docker suite starts stock base /init without DOCKER_MODS/INSTALL_PACKAGES. Its success cannot satisfy complete existing SAB bootstrap acceptance.
sab_complete_mod_acceptance.stock_offline_mod_path: Captured /docker-mods lines 383-410 support offline fallback to an existing /modcache/${FILENAME}.tar.xz. For this pin FILENAME is linuxserver.mods.universal-package-install.ae68d698c8745c48cd634e807eca41a57a2aacb142bee4ca6a2c3b2b6c64afaf. The offline branch accepts an existing valid tar without fetching/verifying a remote layer digest, so a prepared blob would need independent binding to the exact pinned mod manifest/layer before use.
sab_complete_mod_acceptance.offline_package_limit: The captured init-mods-package-install/run uses apk add --no-cache with the requested ffmpeg package. A cached mod tar does not provide signed APK repository indexes, ffmpeg or the complete dependency closure. No such prepared package input set is supplied here; simply mounting an ordinary apk cache does not establish offline operation for --no-cache.
sab_complete_mod_acceptance.network_requirement: For a genuine clean-vendor-root replay with unchanged repository configuration and no prepared offline package repository, restricted bootstrap networking is required. A separately approved signed local repository/mirror and complete package closure could support offline installation, but would be test-specific repository configuration, not current stock configuration. No network-enabled execution or alternate bootstrap is implemented.
sab_complete_mod_acceptance.conditional_ca_conflict: The Alpine ca-certificates refresh executable /usr/sbin/update-ca-certificates rewrites /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt and subject-hash aliases; apk trigger invocation would conflict with the read-only cert-directory mount. Installing/upgrading CA source packages could also write the read-only /usr/share/ca-certificates tree. The actual ffmpeg dependency transaction and trigger invocation have not been captured, so this report does not assert that ffmpeg always triggers CA regeneration.
required_observations: Exact pinned vendor SAB image and exact pinned universal-package-install mod; original /init and both existing environment values, with ephemeral empty config and no user media/config.
No pre-applied mod marker, preinstalled-ffmpeg shortcut, skipped mod, stubbed package installer, altered application startup or removed ffmpeg requirement.
Capture actual package/trigger exit statuses and bounded public initialization evidence, without secrets; demonstrate ffmpeg and ffprobe available and working.

Verify original HTTP/auth readiness and unchanged codec/bootstrap behavior; verify canonical eleven SPKIs absent from all public OS/application stores, native Python and certifi contexts after the entire mod/package stage.

Test whether any CA package trigger/update-ca-certificates operation fails against the read-only trust mounts and whether vendor bootstrap wrongly continues after package failure. Any such incompatibility remains a blocker, not permission to make trust writable or ignore errors.
Require separate approval before any restricted network-enabled isolated bootstrap. No cluster/storage/deployment/publication operations.
